sections.label: How Revenue Is Recorded
sections.note: Commission income is recorded before agent splits, and agent splits, referral fees and brokerage split and fees are all costs. The production file agrees: every month's commission income matches that month's GCI. Splits % and Brokerage % are each a share of commission income.
math: Splits vary from 46.0% to 65.0% of commission income (typical 58.0%). Months with more referral-fee deals or more of the team leader's own deals can run lower. The production file matches every month, so this doesn't point to a recording problem.

Brokerage split and fees dropped. About 6.0% of commission income from January to April, then May 3.2%, June 2.1%, July 1.9%, August 2.2%, September 1.9% (the rows marked Watch). That can mean the team or its agents reached a brokerage cap, the fee schedule changed, or something is missing from the account. Only the broker knows the cap terms, so it goes to the broker as a question, along with when the cap year resets.

sections.label: Company Dollar and Margin
sections.finding: The team kept $41,233 on $339,367 of company dollar, a 12.1% margin.
sections.note: Company dollar = commission income - agent splits - referral fees paid - brokerage split and fees. Margin = net income / company dollar. Operating expenses stayed between $31,731 and $36,421 a month. Profit follows company dollar: the first quarter's company dollar of $22,799 to $26,300 a month didn't cover expenses. The team also collected 6,750.00 in fees charged to agents (Agent Fee Income), outside company dollar.

sections.label: Cost per Closing and Lead Sources
sections.finding: From the 77 closed deals in the export: operating expenses per closing = 304,883.76 / 77 = 3,959.53.
sections.note: Lanternfly Leads is pay at close: its referral fees ($75,197) are its cost, and the team's share is already after them, so the team kept 0.62 per $1 of fees. Pumpkinpatch Portal and Google PPC are paid up front; their spend is the P&L account with the same name. Spend in one month often produces closings months later, so treat this as a rough nine-month view, not a verdict on any source.

items.text: Our brokerage split and fees were 6.0% of commission income from January to April 2026, 3.2% in May and 1.9% to 2.2% from June to September. Did the team or its agents reach a cap in May, or did the fee schedule change? When does the cap year reset?

drafts.label: Owner Brief
drafts.to: You, and a partner if you share it
drafts.subject: Owner Brief: Pinecone & Puddle Home Team P&L, January to September 2026
drafts.body:
Bottom Line: We kept $41,233 in net income for January to September, a 12.1% margin on company dollar, and $19,091 in September (36.9%), after losses in January, February and March. Brokerage split and fees fell from 6.0% of commission income in January to April to between 1.9% and 3.2% from May on. Our decision: keep or cancel Pumpkinpatch Portal at 3,000.00 a month.

Profit: Period net income $41,233 on company dollar of $339,367 (12.1%). September net income $19,091 on company dollar of $51,747 (36.9%).

How Revenue Is Recorded: Gross every month, and it matches our closed-deal export month by month.

Where the Money Goes: People 54.5% of company dollar, occupancy 11.7%, lead generation 11.2%.

What Changed: Company dollar rose from $45,136 in August to $51,747 in September; Google PPC came back down from its August jump.

What Needs a Look:
- Brokerage fees down since May: asking the broker whether we reached a cap or the fee schedule changed.
- 486.20 uncategorized in July.
- Video Editing App, new at 79.00 a month since June.
- Google PPC at 3,940.85 in August.

Cost per Closing: 3,959.53 in operating expenses per closing across 77 closings, with 4,407.36 of company dollar and 535.49 of net income per closing.

Lead Sources: Google PPC returned 3.54 per $1 spent and Pumpkinpatch Portal 1.79; Lanternfly Leads kept 0.62 per $1 of referral fees.

The Decision: Keep or cancel Pumpkinpatch Portal (3,000.00 a month since July; it was 2,500.00). For January to September it cost 24,000.00 and its 16 closings brought the team 66,930.64.

With the Bookkeeper: 4 questions sent; 1 question for the broker.

drafts.label: Email to the Bookkeeper
drafts.subject: Questions On The January To September P&L
drafts.body:
Hi [Bookkeeper Name],

I went through the January to September P&L against our closed-deal export. A few questions:

1. Uncategorized Expense has 486.20 in July. What is it, and where should it go?
2. Video Editing App started in June at 79.00 a month. Which subscription is it?
3. Google PPC was 3,940.85 in August, well above its usual month. Was that one campaign, or a billing catch-up?
4. Brokerage split and fees dropped to 3.2% of commission income in May and 1.9% to 2.2% since, from 6.0% before. Is anything missing from that account from May on?

Once the July item is moved, could you send an updated P&L by month as Excel?

Thanks,
[Owner Name]
